title: nazm.context/2
description: One source definition's semantic context, from `nazm context --json` and the `nazm-mcp` tool `semantic_context`: its exact source and compact links to what the compiler knows it is connected to, in the compilation of one root. `status` is `available` with every section, or `unavailable` with a `reason` and no other section. Paths are relative to the compilation's source root; byte offsets are into the named file. Nothing session-local is included, so the same sources and query give the same bytes. `/2` (N36): a function's `effects` are the compiler's, where `/1` reported them unsupported.

reason.description: Why there is no packet: the file is not one the compilation loaded; the offset is past its end; not on a name; on a name that is not a function, record or enum declared from source; or some file needed syntax recovery or could not be loaded. Present only when `status` is `unavailable`.

dependencies.description: Every entity the declaration uses, other than its own locals, parameters and bindings and the target itself, each once with every occurrence. Ordered by kind, then declaration, then identity.

related_types.description: The records and enums whose names the declaration writes — as a type, a construction's head or a variant's enum — directly, not a transitive closure, with those written occurrences.

references.description: Every use of the target in the compilation, ordered by file then offset. The declaration is not among them: it is `target.source`.

diagnostics.description: The compiler's diagnostics whose primary span is inside the declaration.

effects.description: A function's effects, from the effect checker (N36); null for a record or an enum, and for a function whose body this compilation did not check.

definition.description: The durable definition key, `module::kind name`. Null only where the declaring module has no durable key (a file reached outside the source root); the entity's place is still given, so null never stands in for a location.

member.description: A field's, a variant's or (`Variant.field`) a payload field's name within that definition; null for the definition itself.

fields.description: A record's fields in canonical order; null otherwise.

variants.description: An enum's variants and payloads in canonical order; null otherwise.

text.description: The declaration exactly as it is in the file, byte for byte.

declaration.description: Where its name is declared, in a file of the compilation. An entity with no such declaration — the core prelude's, a built-in's — is not a link: it may shape checking, and is omitted.

calls.description: Each call's callee name, in the calling function's file.

status.description: `not_applicable` for a record or an enum, which calls nothing and is called by nothing.

items.description: Every direct call, grouped by the function at the other end; null when not applicable.

fixes.description: How many fixes the compiler attached.

effect_names.description: A set of effects, each once, in effect-id order: `io`, then `spawn`.

declared.description: Its written `! { … }`; null where it declares none. `[]` is `! {}`: pure.

required.description: What its body requires: the least fixed point over the compilation's resolved calls.

published.description: What a caller in another module must assume: the declared set, or every effect where none is declared.

reasons.description: One per required effect, in effect-id order: the first call or `spawn` in the body that requires it.

source.description: A built-in that exercises it; a `spawn`; a function of this module whose inferred set has it; a function whose declared set has it; or a function of another module that declares no set.

builtin.description: The built-in's name, for `builtin`: compiler-owned, with no source.

availability.description: Sections the compiler has no facts for. `unsupported` means not known — never that none exist.
